isotope.quote: AMoRE searches for the signature of neutrinoless double beta decay of $^{100}$Mo with a 100 kg sample of enriched $^{100}$Mo.

temperature.quote: we have maintained the detector tower at 12 mK during science runs for long-term data collection

total_mass.note: Thirteen CaMoO4 and five Li2MoO4 crystals.
total_mass.quote: for a total crystal mass of 6.2 kg

summary.plain: AMoRE-I was the second stage of AMoRE: eighteen molybdate crystals (6.2 kg), cooled to about 12 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, run at the Yangyang laboratory from 2019 to 2023. It saw no sign of neutrinoless double beta decay of molybdenum-100 and set a lower limit of 2.9 x 10^24 years on its half-life.
summary.technical: 13 48depl-Ca100MoO4 + 5 Li2 100MoO4 crystals (6.2 kg) with MMC readout at ~12 mK in the A5 tunnel of Y2L (700 m); full 18-crystal DAQ December 2020 - April 2023 at 93% live time; exposure 8.02 kg yr (3.89 kg yr of 100Mo), background 0.025 +/- 0.002 counts/keV/kg/yr near Q; T1/2(0vbb, 100Mo) > 2.9e24 yr (90% C.L.), m_bb < 210-610 meV.

technology.quote: Scintillating molybdate crystals coupled with a metallic magnetic calorimeter operate at milli-Kelvin temperatures to measure the energy of electrons emitted in the decay.
technology.value: Eighteen molybdate crystals (CaMoO4 and Li2MoO4) with metallic-magnetic-calorimeter heat and light readout at mK temperatures
